# Architecture: where requirements become design

Requirements describe obligations; architecture explains how the product is organized to satisfy them. Quarto-Needs keeps those concerns distinct and links them explicitly.

## System and its context

::: {.need #SYS-QUARTO-NEEDS type="system" status="approved" tags="architecture;c4"}
## Quarto-Needs

The engineering-traceability tool this case study documents: a requirements/decisions/risk/test/evidence graph authored in Quarto Markdown, analyzed by a Python core, and presented through a Quarto extension.
:::

::: {.need #ACTOR-ENGINEER type="actor" status="approved" tags="architecture;c4" depends-on="SYS-QUARTO-NEEDS"}
## Requirements engineer

Authors, reviews, and approves engineering objects; reads generated views to understand traceability and coverage.
:::

::: {.need #EXT-GITHUB type="external-system" status="approved" tags="architecture;c4;github" depends-on="SYS-QUARTO-NEEDS"}
## GitHub

Hosts the project's issues, which Quarto-Needs federates as read-only, provenance-bound external observations (see `interoperability.qmd`).
:::

::: {.need #EXT-OSLC type="external-system" status="approved" tags="architecture;c4;oslc" depends-on="SYS-QUARTO-NEEDS"}
## OSLC-compliant requirements management tool

An external OSLC Requirements Management provider Quarto-Needs federates from as a read-only, provenance-bound source (see `interoperability.qmd`).
:::

::: {.need #CONTAINER-PYTHON-PKG type="container" status="approved" tags="architecture;c4" technology="Python 3.12" part-of="SYS-QUARTO-NEEDS"}

The installable `quarto-needs` library and CLI: parsing, analysis, governance rules, graph projection, baselines, and localization checks.

## Engineering risks

::: {.need #RISK-001 type="risk" status="approved" priority="critical" tags="semantics;drift;architecture"}
## Semantic meaning diverges across core and presentation layers

Duplicated relation semantics can cause Python, Lua, and JavaScript to disagree about the same engineering graph.
:::

::: {.need #RISK-002 type="risk" status="approved" priority="critical" tags="privacy;security;projection"}
## Public documentation leaks internal source information

Graph or diagnostic projections could accidentally expose absolute paths, arbitrary attributes, or internal source content.
:::

::: {.need #RISK-003 type="risk" status="approved" priority="medium" tags="graph;performance;usability"}
## Large graph projections overwhelm interactive documentation

Unbounded projections can become slow, visually unreadable, and unsuitable for review.
:::

::: {.need #RISK-004 type="risk" status="approved" priority="high" tags="localization;semantics;drift"}
## Translations create a competing engineering model

Localized files can silently diverge from canonical IDs, metadata, and relations unless semantic parity is enforced.
:::

## Architecture decisions

::: {.need #ADR-001 type="architecture-decision" status="accepted" date="2026-08-29" revisit-after="2027-08-29" decision-makers="Quarto-Needs maintainers" tags="python;semantics;architecture" addresses="SYS-001;SYS-003;NFR-005;RISK-001" applies-to="COMP-ANALYSIS;IF-002" confirmed-by="TC-001;TC-008"}
## Keep Python as the semantic authority

### Context and Problem Statement

The product has a Python analysis core, Lua rendering filters, and JavaScript interaction. If each layer defines engineering meaning independently, equivalent views can drift.

### Decision Drivers

- one source of engineering semantics;
- deterministic analysis;
- testability outside the browser;
- presentation layers that remain replaceable.

### Considered Options

- duplicate relation maps in every client;
- resolve semantics in Lua during rendering;
- resolve semantics once in Python and publish semantic projections.

### Decision Outcome

Python owns engineering semantics. Lua and JavaScript consume relation metadata and other semantic projections emitted by the core.

### Consequences

Public projection contracts become more important, but presentation clients become simpler and cannot silently redefine engineering meaning.

### Confirmation

`TC-001` confirms the canonical snapshot and `TC-008` confirms relation-catalog semantics.
:::

::: {.need #ADR-002 type="architecture-decision" status="accepted" date="2026-08-29" revisit-after="2027-08-29" decision-makers="Quarto-Needs maintainers" tags="quarto;documentation;architecture" addresses="SYS-002;NFR-003" applies-to="COMP-EXTENSION;IF-001" confirmed-by="TC-002"}
## Use Quarto as the executable documentation interface

### Context and Problem Statement

The engineering model needs both formal structure and high-quality human explanation.

### Decision Drivers

- text and Git workflows;
- publishable documentation;
- Markdown narrative;
- extension-based generated views.

### Decision Outcome

Use Quarto documents as the authoring and publishing interface while keeping engineering semantics in the Python core.

### Consequences

The product remains compatible with ordinary documentation workflows and can progressively enhance HTML without making HTML the source of truth.

### Confirmation

`TC-002` renders the book and verifies the static/progressive presentation path.
:::

::: {.need #ADR-003 type="architecture-decision" status="accepted" date="2026-08-29" revisit-after="2027-08-29" decision-makers="Quarto-Needs maintainers" tags="graph;model;traceability" addresses="SYS-001;FUN-002" applies-to="COMP-ANALYSIS;IF-002" confirmed-by="TC-008"}
## Model traceability as a typed property graph

### Context and Problem Statement

Requirements, decisions, risks, implementation, tests, and evidence need a common relationship model without collapsing their distinct meanings.

### Decision Outcome

Represent engineering objects as typed nodes and engineering relations as typed edges with canonical semantic families and directions.

### Consequences

Traceability, impact analysis, queries, and generated views can operate over one model while object roles remain explicit.

### Confirmation

`TC-008` verifies the relation catalog and canonical semantic projection.
:::

::: {.need #ADR-004 type="architecture-decision" status="accepted" date="2026-08-29" revisit-after="2027-08-29" decision-makers="Quarto-Needs maintainers" tags="graph;progressive-enhancement;accessibility" addresses="SYS-006;NFR-003;FUN-004" applies-to="COMP-GRAPH;COMP-EXTENSION;IF-003" confirmed-by="TC-006;TC-010"}
## Drive static and interactive graphs from the same projection

### Context and Problem Statement

Separate graph-generation paths can cause the accessible static representation and the interactive Cytoscape view to disagree.

### Decision Outcome

Generate one bounded public projection and derive static diagram/table output and interactive exploration from that same artifact.

### Consequences

The public graph schema becomes a stable contract and interactive features must operate as progressive enhancement over it.

### Confirmation

`TC-006` validates the public projection contract and `TC-010` checks the exploration assets.
:::

::: {.need #ADR-005 type="architecture-decision" status="accepted" date="2026-08-29" revisit-after="2027-08-29" decision-makers="Quarto-Needs maintainers" tags="localization;i18n;semantics" addresses="SYS-005;FUN-006;RISK-004" applies-to="COMP-I18N" confirmed-by="TC-005"}
## Keep English canonical and localization presentation-only

### Context and Problem Statement

A multilingual book should not create two engineering graphs that can evolve independently.

### Decision Outcome

English QMD files are canonical engineering sources; `*.pt-BR.qmd` siblings may translate presentation text only. Pre-render validation rejects semantic differences.

### Consequences

Translations remain useful to readers while governance, baselines, impact analysis, and machine-readable exports stay language-neutral.

### Confirmation

`TC-005` checks semantic parity and localized title projection generation.
:::

::: {.need #ADR-006 type="architecture-decision" status="accepted" date="2026-08-29" revisit-after="2027-08-29" decision-makers="Quarto-Needs maintainers" tags="query;graph;views" addresses="FUN-003" applies-to="COMP-ANALYSIS;COMP-GRAPH" confirmed-by="TC-009"}
## Evaluate named queries in the core and materialize reusable views

### Context and Problem Statement

Reimplementing query semantics in Lua would create another semantic authority and make graph views harder to reproduce.

### Decision Outcome

Named queries are evaluated by the Python core. Their result sets can be materialized as bounded graph views and consumed by shortcodes through a view manifest.

### Consequences

Selection remains deterministic and reusable across tables and graphs; presentation layers only request an already resolved view.

### Confirmation

`TC-009` verifies named-query graph materialization and manifest resolution.
:::

::: {.need #ADR-007 type="architecture-decision" status="accepted" date="2026-08-30" revisit-after="2027-08-30" decision-makers="Quarto-Needs maintainers" tags="quarto;toc;sidebar;usability;progressive-enhancement" addresses="FUN-009" applies-to="COMP-EXTENSION" confirmed-by="TC-014"}
## Treat the margin TOC control as persistent progressive enhancement

### Context and Problem Statement

The page margin TOC can consume useful reading width, but a collapse control positioned over the TOC undermines the navigation it is intended to improve.

### Decision Drivers

- preserve native Quarto navigation semantics;
- make the feature optional and browser-only;
- persist the reader's collapsed state;
- reclaim content width while collapsed;
- never obscure the expanded TOC with the control itself.

### Decision Outcome

Implement the control as JavaScript progressive enhancement. Persist state in local storage, use Quarto's `fullcontent` class only while the extension forces the collapsed state, and position the expanded control completely outside the margin sidebar with an explicit gap.

### Consequences

The static document remains usable without JavaScript, while HTML readers gain a persistent space-reclaiming control. Positioning becomes an explicit regression contract rather than incidental CSS/DOM behavior.

### Confirmation

`TC-014` checks persistence/full-content behavior and verifies that the expanded control is positioned by `button.offsetWidth + gap`, never by the old half-width overlap.
:::
